subject: Architecture
title: St. Peter's Basilica: Biggest Church on Earth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on St. Peter's Basilica: Biggest Church on Earth.

hook.text: St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City is the largest church ever built — it can hold 20,000 worshippers.

buildup.text: Construction lasted 120 years. Bramante, Raphael, and Michelangelo all served as lead architects.

discovery.text: Michelangelo designed the dome at age 71. He refused payment — calling it his service to God.

twist.text: To fund construction, the Pope sold 'indulgences' — forgiveness for sins. This triggered the Protestant Reformation.

climax.text: The dome rises 448 feet and inspired the U.S. Capitol, St. Paul's in London, and dozens of other domes.

punchline.text: One church's construction bill split Christianity in two.

quiz.question: What unintended consequence came from funding St. Peter's construction?
options: The Vatican went bankrupt for decades
Selling indulgences helped trigger the Protestant Reformation
Rome's population declined as workers left the city

details.summary: St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City, completed in 1626 after 120 years of construction, is the world's largest church at 15,160 square meters. Michelangelo redesigned its dome (136 meters tall).
details.whyItMatters: St. Peter's demonstrates that monumental sacred architecture requires multi-generational commitment. No single architect, pope, or generation completed it.
takeaways: World's largest church at 15,160 square meters, 120 years to build
Michelangelo redesigned the 136-meter dome as centerpiece
Bernini's colonnade and baldachin define the interior and exterior

faq.question: How many architects worked on St. Peter's?
faq.answer: At least six principal architects across 120 years: Bramante (original plan), Raphael, Peruzzi, Sangallo the Younger, Michelangelo (who redesigned the dome), Maderno (who extended the nave), and Bernini (who designed the interior decorations and piazza colonnade).

faq.question: Why is the interior so enormous?
faq.answer: Scale communicates the power and authority of the Catholic Church. The basilica was deliberately designed to overwhelm visitors with its vastness — brass markers in the floor show that other great cathedrals would fit within its nave. Every element is oversized to create a sense of divine grandeur.
